prompt: A particle on the half-line has $\psi(x)=A\,x\,e^{-x/a}$ for $x\ge0$ and $\psi=0$ for $x<0$, with $a>0$ and $A$ real. Find the probability of finding it at $x>2a$.

why: lost the $u^2$ term when integrating by parts

hints: Normalise first, then integrate $|\psi|^2$ with the substitution $u=2x/a$.

prompt: A particle is in the $n=3$ stationary state of an infinite well $0<x<L$. Find the probability of finding it in $0<x<L/4$.

rubric.text: Evaluate the sine at $3\pi/2$ and combine

solution:
$\psi_3=\sqrt{2/L}\,\sin(3\pi x/L)$ (inf-well).
$P=\int_0^{L/4}\tfrac2L\sin^2\!\tfrac{3\pi x}{L}dx$ (born).
$=\tfrac1L\int_0^{L/4}\!\big(1-\cos\tfrac{6\pi x}{L}\big)dx=\tfrac14-\tfrac{1}{6\pi}\sin\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$.
$\sin(3\pi/2)=-1$, so $P=\tfrac14+\tfrac1{6\pi}\approx0.303$.
hints: Use the half-angle identity; the sine at $3\pi/2$ is $-1$, not $0$.

prompt: An electron ($m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\hbar=1.05\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$, $q=1.60\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$) has the stationary state $\psi=Ae^{-x^2/2b^2}$ with energy $E=\hbar^2/(2mb^2)$, where $b=0.50\ \mathrm{nm}$, in an even potential that is a pure parabola $V=\tfrac12m\omega^2x^2$. Find $\hbar\omega$ in eV.

rubric.text: Match to $\tfrac12m\omega^2x^2$ and convert to eV

solution:
$\psi''/\psi=x^2/b^4-1/b^2$ (tise).
$V=E+\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\psi''/\psi=\dfrac{\hbar^2x^2}{2mb^4}$ (tise).
Compare with $\tfrac12m\omega^2x^2$: $\omega=\hbar/(mb^2)$ (qho).
$\hbar\omega=\hbar^2/(mb^2)=4.84\times10^{-20}\ \mathrm J\approx0.30\ \mathrm{eV}$.
hints: Insert $\psi$ into $-\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\psi''+V\psi=E\psi$ and solve for $V$.

prompt: An electron ($m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\hbar=1.05\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$, $q=1.60\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$) sits in $V(x)=-\alpha\,\delta(x)$ with $\alpha=0.20\ \mathrm{eV\,nm}$. Its single bound state is $\psi\propto e^{-\kappa|x|}$. Find the rms position $\sqrt{\langle x^2\rangle}$ in nm.

rubric.text: Derivative jump at the delta gives $\kappa=m\alpha/\hbar^2$
Numbers: $\alpha$ in J m, then nm

solution:
Integrate the Schrodinger equation across $x=0$: $\Delta\psi'=-\tfrac{2m\alpha}{\hbar^2}\psi(0)$ (tise).
With $\psi'$ jumping by $-2\kappa\psi(0)$: $\kappa=m\alpha/\hbar^2$.
$|\psi|^2=\kappa e^{-2\kappa|x|}$; $\langle x^2\rangle=2\kappa\!\int_0^\infty x^2e^{-2\kappa x}dx=1/(2\kappa^2)$ (born).
$\alpha=3.2\times10^{-29}\ \mathrm{J\,m}$, $\kappa=2.64\times10^{9}\ \mathrm{m^{-1}}$.
$x_{rms}=1/(\sqrt2\kappa)\approx0.27\ \mathrm{nm}$.
hints: The jump in $\psi'$ across the delta fixes $\kappa$.

prompt: A particle is in the ground state of an infinite well $0<x<L$. The right wall is moved instantly to $x=2L$. Find the probability that the particle is then in the ground state of the enlarged well.

why: new ground state normalised with $2/L$ instead of $1/L$
dropped the $\sqrt2$ from the two normalisations

rubric.text: Sudden change: wavefunction unchanged, so probability is $|\langle\phi_1|\psi_1\rangle|^2$

solution:
Instant move leaves $\psi_1=\sqrt{2/L}\sin(\pi x/L)$ on $[0,L]$ (inf-well).
New ground state $\phi_1=\sqrt{1/L}\sin(\pi x/2L)$ on $[0,2L]$.
Overlap $=\tfrac{\sqrt2}{L}\int_0^L\sin\tfrac{\pi x}{L}\sin\tfrac{\pi x}{2L}dx$ (dirac).
Integral $=\tfrac12\big[\tfrac{2L}\pi+\tfrac{2L}{3\pi}\big]=\tfrac{4L}{3\pi}$.
Overlap $=\dfrac{4\sqrt2}{3\pi}$; probability $=\dfrac{32}{9\pi^2}\approx0.36$.
hints: The state does not change in a sudden move; project it onto the new ground state.

prompt: An electron ($m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $h=6.63\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$, $c=3.00\times10^8\ \mathrm{m/s}$) in an infinite well absorbs a photon of wavelength $620\ \mathrm{nm}$ and goes from $n=2$ to $n=3$ exactly. Find the well width $L$ in nm.
solution:
$E_\gamma=hc/\lambda=3.21\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm J\approx2.0\ \mathrm{eV}$ (units).
$E_n=n^2h^2/(8mL^2)$, so $E_3-E_2=5E_1$ (inf-well).
$E_1=E_\gamma/5=6.42\times10^{-20}\ \mathrm J$.
$L=h/\sqrt{8mE_1}\approx9.7\times10^{-10}\ \mathrm m=0.97\ \mathrm{nm}$.
hints: Energy gap between $n=2$ and $n=3$ is $5E_1$.

prompt: Particles of energy $E=2V_0$ move in from $x<0$ where $V=0$ and meet a step $V=V_0$ for $x>0$. Find the transmission probability, defined by probability flux.

why: used the reflection amplitude, not its square, in $T=1-R$
squared the transmitted amplitude and forgot the flux factor $k_2/k_1$ (exceeds 1)

rubric.text: Match $\psi,\psi'$ at the step to get $r=(k_1-k_2)/(k_1+k_2)$

solution:
$k_1\propto\sqrt{E}$, $k_2\propto\sqrt{E-V_0}$, so $k_2/k_1=1/\sqrt2$ (step-tunnel).
Continuity of $\psi$ and $\psi'$: $r=(k_1-k_2)/(k_1+k_2)=(\sqrt2-1)/(\sqrt2+1)=3-2\sqrt2$ (tise).
$R=r^2=17-12\sqrt2\approx0.029$.
$T=1-R=12\sqrt2-16\approx0.97$ (flux conservation).
hints: Match $\psi$ and $\psi'$; transmission is $1-R$.

prompt: An electron ($m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\hbar=1.05\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$, $q=1.60\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$) tunnels through a rectangular barrier whose top is $2.0\ \mathrm{eV}$ above its energy. In the thick-barrier limit $T\propto e^{-2\kappa a}$. By what factor does $T$ fall when the width $a$ goes from $0.20\ \mathrm{nm}$ to $0.40\ \mathrm{nm}$?
solution:
$\kappa=\sqrt{2m(V_0-E)}/\hbar$ with $V_0-E=3.2\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm J$ (step-tunnel).
$\kappa\approx7.27\times10^{9}\ \mathrm{m^{-1}}$.
Same prefactor, so $T_1/T_2=e^{2\kappa(0.20\ \mathrm{nm})}$ (scaling).
Exponent $=2.91$; factor $\approx18$.
hints: The prefactor cancels in the ratio; only the exponent difference matters.

prompt: In the oscillator ground state $\psi_0\propto e^{-\xi^2/2}$ with $\xi=x\sqrt{m\omega/\hbar}$, find the probability of finding the particle outside the classical turning points. Give the dimensionless number.
solution:
$E_0=\tfrac12\hbar\omega=\tfrac12 m\omega^2x_t^2$ gives $\xi_t=1$ (qho).
$|\psi_0|^2=\pi^{-1/2}e^{-\xi^2}$ (born).
$P=2\int_1^\infty\pi^{-1/2}e^{-\xi^2}d\xi=\mathrm{erfc}(1)$.
$P\approx0.157$.
hints: Find $\xi$ at which $E_0=V$; then integrate the Gaussian tails.

prompt: An oscillator is in $|\psi\rangle=(|0\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ with real standard $|n\rangle$ ($a|n\rangle=\sqrt n|n-1\rangle$). Find $\langle x^2\rangle$ in units of $\hbar/(m\omega)$.

why: sign error on the cross term

solution:
$x^2=\tfrac{\hbar}{2m\omega}(a^2+a^{\dagger2}+2a^\dagger a+1)$ (operators).
$\langle0|x^2|0\rangle=\tfrac12$, $\langle2|x^2|2\rangle=\tfrac52$ (qho).
$\langle0|x^2|2\rangle=\tfrac12\langle0|a^2|2\rangle=\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$ (dirac).
$\langle x^2\rangle=\tfrac12\big(\tfrac12+\tfrac52\big)+2\cdot\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt2}2=\tfrac{3+\sqrt2}{2}$.
hints: Interference between $|0\rangle$ and $|2\rangle$ enters through $a^2$ and $a^{\dagger2}$.

prompt: A particle with $H=p^2/2m+\lambda x^4$ ($\lambda>0$) is in a stationary state. Find $\langle T\rangle/\langle V\rangle$.

why: dropped the factor 2 in $2\langle T\rangle=\langle xV'\rangle$

rubric.text: Stationary: zero, so $2\langle T\rangle=\langle xV'\rangle=4\langle V\rangle$

solution:
$d\langle xp\rangle/dt=\langle 2T-xV'\rangle$ (operators).
A stationary state has $d\langle A\rangle/dt=0$, so $2\langle T\rangle=\langle x\,dV/dx\rangle$ (hamiltonian).
$x\,dV/dx=4\lambda x^4=4V$.
$\langle T\rangle=2\langle V\rangle$; ratio $2$.
hints: Use the time derivative of $\langle xp\rangle$ in a stationary state.

prompt: For $H=p^2/2m+V(x)$ and ground state $|0\rangle$, expand $\langle0|[x,[x,H]]|0\rangle$ over energy eigenstates. For a harmonic oscillator only $|1\rangle$ has $\langle n|x|0\rangle\ne0$. Find $|\langle1|x|0\rangle|^2$.

why: missed the factor $\tfrac12$ in the sum rule
factor 2 slip in the double commutator
gave the amplitude $|\langle1|x|0\rangle|$ shape, not its square

solution:
$[x,H]=i\hbar p/m$, so $[x,[x,H]]=(i\hbar/m)(i\hbar)=-\hbar^2/m$ (operators).
Insert $\sum|n\rangle\langle n|$: $\langle0|[x,[x,H]]|0\rangle=-2\sum_n(E_n-E_0)|\langle n|x|0\rangle|^2$ (dirac).
So $\sum_n(E_n-E_0)|x_{n0}|^2=\hbar^2/2m$.
Only $n=1$, gap $\hbar\omega$ (qho): $|x_{10}|^2=\dfrac{\hbar}{2m\omega}$.
hints: Expand the double commutator in a complete set; all $n\ne1$ drop out.

prompt: An electron ($m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\hbar=1.05\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$, $q=1.60\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$) has $\langle p\rangle=0$ and position spread $\Delta x=0.10\ \mathrm{nm}$. Using $\Delta x\,\Delta p\ge\hbar/2$, find the smallest possible $\langle p^2\rangle/2m$ in eV.
solution:
$\langle p\rangle=0$ gives $\langle p^2\rangle=(\Delta p)^2$ (uncertainty).
$\Delta p\ge\hbar/(2\Delta x)$.
$K_{min}=\hbar^2/(8m\,\Delta x^2)=1.51\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm J$ (estimate).
$\approx0.95\ \mathrm{eV}$.
hints: Remember the $\hbar/2$ bound, not $\hbar$.

prompt: A spin-$\tfrac12$ particle is in the eigenstate of $S_x$ with eigenvalue $+\hbar/2$. Find $\Delta S_y\,\Delta S_z$ in units of $\hbar^2$.

why: assumed an $S_x$ eigenstate has no spread in any component
forgot the $\tfrac12$ in the Robertson bound and took $\hbar^2/2$

solution:
$\langle S_y\rangle=\langle S_z\rangle=0$ in $|{+x}\rangle$ (spin-half).
$S_i^2=\hbar^2/4$, so $\Delta S_y=\Delta S_z=\hbar/2$.
Product $=\hbar^2/4$.
Bound: $\tfrac12\hbar|\langle S_x\rangle|=\hbar^2/4$ (uncertainty), so it saturates.
hints: Each component squared is $\hbar^2/4$; subtract the squared mean.

prompt: A system with orthonormal energy eigenstates $|1\rangle,|2\rangle,|3\rangle$ of energies $E,2E,3E$ is in $|\psi\rangle=(|1\rangle+i|2\rangle+2|3\rangle)/\sqrt6$. Find the energy spread $\Delta E=\sqrt{\langle H^2\rangle-\langle H\rangle^2}$.
solution:
$|c_n|^2=\tfrac16,\tfrac16,\tfrac23$ (born); the phase $i$ drops out.
$\langle H\rangle=\tfrac16(1)+\tfrac16(2)+\tfrac46(3)=\tfrac52$ in units of $E$ (dirac).
$\langle H^2\rangle=\tfrac16(1)+\tfrac16(4)+\tfrac46(9)=\tfrac{41}6$.
$\mathrm{Var}=\tfrac{41}6-\tfrac{25}4=\tfrac7{12}$; $\Delta E=\sqrt{7/12}\,E$.
hints: Use the squared amplitudes as weights for $E$ and $E^2$.

prompt: At $t=0$ an oscillator is in $(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$, with real standard $|n\rangle$ so $\langle0|x|1\rangle=+\sqrt{\hbar/2m\omega}$. Let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/m\omega}$ and period $T=2\pi/\omega$. Find $\langle x\rangle$ at $t=T/6$.

why: extra factor $\tfrac12$ in the cross term

solution:
$|\psi(t)\rangle=(|0\rangle+e^{-i\omega t}|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ (time-evol).
$\langle x\rangle=2\cdot\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\cos\omega t=\tfrac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\cos\omega t$ (dirac).
At $t=T/6$, $\omega t=\pi/3$, $\cos=\tfrac12$.
$\langle x\rangle=\ell/(2\sqrt2)$.
hints: Only the relative phase $e^{-i\omega t}$ between $|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$ matters.

prompt: Spin-$\tfrac12$ particles prepared in $S_z=+\hbar/2$ pass first an analyser along $\hat n$, lying in the $xz$-plane at $60^\circ$ to $+z$, keeping the $+$ output. They then meet an analyser along $z$ that keeps the $-$ output. Find the probability that a particle entering the first analyser leaves the second.

why: assumed the intermediate stage randomises (so $\tfrac12$) times $\cos^2$

solution:
Angle between spin axes is $\theta$; overlap probability for same sign is $\cos^2(\theta/2)$ (spin-half).
Stage 1: $\cos^2 30^\circ=\tfrac34$.
Stage 2: $|{+n}\rangle\to|{-z}\rangle$ has $\sin^2 30^\circ=\tfrac14$ (born).
Product $=\tfrac3{16}$.
hints: Use half the angle between axes: $\cos^2(\theta/2)$ for the same sign, $\sin^2$ for opposite.

prompt: An electron ($g=2$, so the Larmor angular frequency is $\omega_L=qB/m_e$; $q=1.60\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$, $m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$) has spin along $+x$ at $t=0$ in $B=0.50\ \mathrm T$ along $z$. Find the first time at which $\langle S_x\rangle=-\hbar/2$, in ps.

rubric.text: Reversal of $\langle S_x\rangle$ requires a rotation of $\pi$

solution:
$\omega_L=qB/m=8.78\times10^{10}\ \mathrm{rad/s}$ (spin-half, lorentz).
$\langle\vec S\rangle$ precesses about $z$ at $\omega_L$.
$\langle S_x\rangle=\tfrac\hbar2\cos\omega_Lt$ reaches $-\hbar/2$ at $\omega_Lt=\pi$.
$t=\pi/\omega_L\approx3.6\times10^{-11}\ \mathrm s=36\ \mathrm{ps}$.
hints: A half turn of precession is needed, not a quarter turn.

prompt: A particle is in $|l=2,m=1\rangle$. Find $\langle L_x^2\rangle$ in units of $\hbar^2$.

rubric.text: Symmetry $\langle L_x^2\rangle=\langle L_y^2\rangle$ in an $L_z$ eigenstate

solution:
$\langle L^2\rangle=l(l+1)\hbar^2=6\hbar^2$ (ang-mom-qm).
$\langle L_z^2\rangle=m^2\hbar^2=\hbar^2$.
$\langle L_x^2\rangle=\langle L_y^2\rangle$ by rotation symmetry about $z$ (operators).
$\langle L_x^2\rangle=\tfrac12(6-1)\hbar^2=\tfrac52\hbar^2$.
hints: Split $L^2-L_z^2$ equally between $x$ and $y$.

prompt: A diatomic molecule is a rigid rotor with $I=1.45\times10^{-46}\ \mathrm{kg\,m^2}$ and $E_l=\hbar^2l(l+1)/2I$. Using $\hbar=1.05\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$, $h=6.63\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$ and $c=3.00\times10^8\ \mathrm{m/s}$, find the wavelength in mm of the photon emitted in the $l=2\to l=1$ transition.
solution:
$E_l=\hbar^2l(l+1)/2I$ gives $E_2=3\hbar^2/I$, $E_1=\hbar^2/I$ (ang-mom-qm).
$\Delta E=2\hbar^2/I=1.52\times10^{-22}\ \mathrm J$ (rot-dynamics).
$\lambda=hc/\Delta E=1.31\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm m$.
$\lambda\approx1.3\ \mathrm{mm}$.
hints: Use $l(l+1)$ for both levels before subtracting.

prompt: An electron ($m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\hbar=1.05\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$) in an infinite well of width $L=1.0\ \mathrm{nm}$ starts in $(\phi_1+\phi_2)/\sqrt2$. Find the period of the oscillation of $\langle x\rangle$ in fs.

rubric.text: Only the $\phi_1$--$\phi_2$ beat survives in $\langle x\rangle$

solution:
$\langle x\rangle$ contains the cross term $\propto\cos[(E_2-E_1)t/\hbar]$ (time-evol).
$E_n=n^2\pi^2\hbar^2/(2mL^2)$, so $E_2-E_1=3E_1$ (inf-well).
$T=2\pi\hbar/(3E_1)=4mL^2/(3\pi\hbar)$.
$T\approx3.7\times10^{-15}\ \mathrm s=3.7\ \mathrm{fs}$.
hints: The oscillation frequency is the energy gap over $\hbar$.

prompt: A free electron ($m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\hbar=1.05\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$) starts as a minimum-uncertainty Gaussian packet with $\Delta x_0=1.0\ \mathrm{nm}$. Its width obeys $\Delta x(t)=\Delta x_0\sqrt{1+(\hbar t/2m\Delta x_0^2)^2}$. Find the time in fs at which $\Delta x=2\Delta x_0$.
solution:
Doubling needs $1+u^2=4$ with $u=\hbar t/2m\Delta x_0^2$ (time-evol).
$u=\sqrt3$.
Spread comes from $\Delta p=\hbar/2\Delta x_0$ (uncertainty); scale $2m\Delta x_0^2/\hbar=1.74\times10^{-14}\ \mathrm s$.
$t=\sqrt3\times17.4\ \mathrm{fs}\approx30\ \mathrm{fs}$.
hints: Doubling means the square root equals 2, not that the bracket equals 2.

prompt: A two-level system has $H=\begin{pmatrix}E_0&A\\A&E_0\end{pmatrix}$ in the basis $(|1\rangle,|2\rangle)$ with $A=0.020\ \mathrm{eV}$. It starts in $|1\rangle$. Using $\hbar=1.05\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$ and $q=1.60\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$, find the first time in fs at which the probability of $|2\rangle$ is $\tfrac12$.
solution:
Eigenstates $(|1\rangle\pm|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $E=E_0\pm A$ (two-level).
$|\psi(t)\rangle\propto\cos(At/\hbar)|1\rangle-i\sin(At/\hbar)|2\rangle$ (time-evol).
$P_2=\sin^2(At/\hbar)=\tfrac12$ gives $At/\hbar=\pi/4$.
$t=\pi\hbar/4A=2.58\times10^{-14}\ \mathrm s\approx26\ \mathrm{fs}$.
hints: Splitting between eigenvalues is $2A$, so the oscillation is $\sin^2(At/\hbar)$.

prompt: A two-level system has $H=\begin{pmatrix}0&\Delta\\\Delta&\varepsilon\end{pmatrix}$ with $\varepsilon=3\Delta$ and starts in the first basis state. Find the maximum probability of ever finding it in the second basis state.

why: probability of staying, not of transferring

solution:
$P_2(t)=\sin^22\theta\,\sin^2(\Omega t/2)$ with $\tan2\theta=2\Delta/\varepsilon$ (two-level).
$\sin^22\theta=\dfrac{4\Delta^2}{4\Delta^2+\varepsilon^2}$ (dirac).
The sine factor reaches 1 at some time, so $P_{max}=\sin^22\theta$.
$\varepsilon=3\Delta$: $P_{max}=4/13$.
hints: Maximum transfer equals $\sin^2$ of the mixing angle $2\theta$.

prompt: An infinite well of width $L=1.5\ \mathrm{nm}$ ($0<x<L$) gets the perturbation $H'=\alpha\,\delta(x-L/3)$ with $\alpha=0.60\ \mathrm{eV\,nm}$. Find the first-order energy shift of the $n=2$ state in eV.
solution:
$E^{(1)}=\langle\psi_2|H'|\psi_2\rangle$ (perturbation).
$=\alpha|\psi_2(L/3)|^2$ (inf-well).
$|\psi_2(L/3)|^2=\tfrac2L\sin^2(2\pi/3)=\tfrac2L\cdot\tfrac34$.
$E^{(1)}=0.60\times\tfrac{3}{2\times1.5}=0.60\ \mathrm{eV}$.
hints: A delta perturbation samples $|\psi|^2$ at one point.

prompt: An oscillator has the perturbation $H'=bx^4$. With $\ell^2=\hbar/(m\omega)$ and $x=\tfrac{\ell}{\sqrt2}(a+a^\dagger)$, find the first-order shift of the $n=1$ level in units of $b\ell^4$.
solution:
$E^{(1)}_n=b\langle n|x^4|n\rangle$ (perturbation).
$x^4=\tfrac{\ell^4}{4}(a+a^\dagger)^4$ (operators).
Keep terms with equal numbers of $a$ and $a^\dagger$: $\langle n|\cdot|n\rangle=6n^2+6n+3$ (qho).
$n=1$: $15$; $E^{(1)}=\tfrac{15}{4}b\ell^4$.
hints: Only terms with two $a$ and two $a^\dagger$ contribute; count them via $6n^2+6n+3$.

prompt: Use the trial function $\psi=e^{-\alpha x^2}$ to bound the ground-state energy of $H=p^2/2m+\lambda x^4$. Take $\langle p^2\rangle/2m=\hbar^2\alpha/2m$ and $\langle x^4\rangle=3/(16\alpha^2)$. The optimum $E$ equals $c\,(\hbar^4\lambda/m^2)^{1/3}$. Find $c$.

why: set $\langle T\rangle=\langle V\rangle$ instead of minimising
doubled kinetic term and used $\langle x^4\rangle=1/16\alpha^2$

solution:
$E(\alpha)=\dfrac{\hbar^2\alpha}{2m}+\dfrac{3\lambda}{16\alpha^2}$ (variational).
$dE/d\alpha=0$: $\dfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}=\dfrac{3\lambda}{8\alpha^3}$, so $\alpha^3=\dfrac{3m\lambda}{4\hbar^2}$.
Then $\dfrac{3\lambda}{16\alpha^2}=\dfrac{\hbar^2\alpha}{4m}$ and $E=\dfrac{3\hbar^2\alpha}{4m}$ (tise).
$E=\tfrac34(\tfrac34)^{1/3}(\hbar^4\lambda/m^2)^{1/3}\approx0.68\,(\hbar^4\lambda/m^2)^{1/3}$.
hints: Minimise over $\alpha$; do not set $T=V$.

prompt: A particle moves in $V=F|x|$ with $F>0$. Using WKB with $\oint p\,dx=(n+\tfrac12)\,2\pi\hbar$ for $n=0,1,2,\dots$, find $E_2/E_0$.
solution:
$\oint p\,dx=4\int_0^{E/F}\sqrt{2m(E-Fx)}\,dx=\dfrac{8\sqrt{2m}}{3F}E^{3/2}$ (variational/WKB).
Set equal to $(n+\tfrac12)2\pi\hbar$: $E\propto(n+\tfrac12)^{2/3}$ (tise).
$E_2/E_0=(2.5/0.5)^{2/3}=5^{2/3}$.
$\approx2.92$.
hints: Phase-space area scales as $E^{3/2}$ for a linear potential.

prompt: Five non-interacting electrons (spin-$\tfrac12$) fill an infinite well of width $L=1.0\ \mathrm{nm}$. The ground state occupies $n=1,1,2,2,3$. Find the lowest nonzero excitation energy of the system in eV (spin flips cost nothing and are ignored), using $m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\hbar=1.05\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$, $q=1.60\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$.

rubric.text: Pauli: at most two electrons per level

solution:
Pauli limits each $n$ to two electrons (identical).
Level $n=3$ has one electron, so it can accept one more.
Options: $2\to3$ costs $(9-4)E_1=5E_1$; $3\to4$ costs $7E_1$; $1\to3$ costs $8E_1$ (inf-well).
Lowest is $5E_1$ with $E_1=\pi^2\hbar^2/2mL^2=0.373\ \mathrm{eV}$; answer $1.87\ \mathrm{eV}$.
hints: A promotion needs an empty slot; level $n=3$ still has one.

prompt: Two identical spin-0 bosons in an infinite well $0<x<L$ occupy $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ in the symmetric state $[\phi_1(x_1)\phi_2(x_2)+\phi_2(x_1)\phi_1(x_2)]/\sqrt2$. Find the probability that both lie in $0<x<L/2$.

rubric.text: Each of $\phi_1,\phi_2$ has probability $\tfrac12$ in the left half

solution:
$P=\tfrac12\iint_{\text{left}}|\phi_1\phi_2'+\phi_2\phi_1'|^2$ expands to direct plus exchange (identical).
Direct: $P_1P_2=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac12=\tfrac14$ (inf-well).
Exchange: $I=\tfrac2L\int_0^{L/2}\sin\tfrac{\pi x}{L}\sin\tfrac{2\pi x}{L}dx=\tfrac{4}{3\pi}$ (dirac).
Bosons add $I^2$: $P=\tfrac14+\tfrac{16}{9\pi^2}\approx0.43$.
hints: The symmetric state adds an exchange term $I^2$ to the product of single-particle probabilities.
